title: Dissection and Tissue Preparation of Spotted Lanternfly for Morphometric Analysis
author: Alina Avanesyan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8tthwnn
materials: 3. Isolate the labium and expose the stylets using a pair of fine tweezers from the micro dissecting kit (BioQuip Products Inc., Rancho Dominguez, CA, USA; micro dissecting kit, Cat. No. 4761). 4. Similarly, separate the tarsus from one of the forelegs using the micro slide tool kit (BioQuip Products Inc., Rancho Dominguez, CA, USA; micro slide tool kit, Cat. No. 4831). Step 3. Morphometric measurements 1. For each individual insect, photograph the head with the mouthparts, the labium, the stylet fascicle, and the dorsal view of the tarsal tip (Zeiss Axio-Imager M1 using Zeiss ZEN imaging software (Carl Zeiss, Jena, Germany)). 2. Using the photographs, take the following 12 morphometric characteristics: 1) Distance from the labial tip to the base of the first labial segment; µm; 2) Distance from the labial tip to the base of the last labial segment; µm; 3) Maximum width of the last labial segment; µm; 4) Distance from the tip of the stylet fascicle to the base of the stylets; µm; 5) Distance from the apex of stylet fascicle extended from labial tip to the labial tip; µm; 6) Distance between tarsal claw tips from the dorsal view; µm; 7) Distance between bending centers of the external arcs of the tarsal claws from the dorsal view; µm; 8) Distance between the lateral margin of the arolium and tarsal claw tips from the dorsal view; µm; 9) Distance between the lateral margin of the arolium and bending centers of the external arcs of the tarsal claws from the dorsal view; µm; 10) The maximum anterior width of the arolium; µm; 11) Length of the lateral margin of the arolium; µm; 12) The angle between the lateral margins of the arolium from the dorsal view; degrees.

steps.title: Collect and preserve insects
steps.instruction: Collect spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) and preserve them for later dissection.

substeps.instruction: Immediately place insects in small glass or plastic vials containing 80% ethanol.
Transport vials to the laboratory and store in the fridge at 4 °C until dissection.

steps.title: Dissect head and tarsi
steps.instruction: Isolate the head and tarsi from the insect body using a dissecting microscope.

substeps.instruction: Place an individual insect on a microscope slide.
Separate the head with the mouthparts from the insect body under the dissecting microscope.
Transfer the isolated mouthparts and tarsi back into 80% ethanol for scanning electron microscopy.

steps.title: Dehydrate specimens
steps.instruction: Perform a graded dehydration of the mouthparts and tarsi using ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Transfer specimens from 80% ethanol to 95% ethanol for 10 min.
Transfer specimens to 100% ethanol three times for 10 min each.

steps.title: Perform HMDS transition
steps.instruction: Transition specimens from ethanol to hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) using a graded series.

substeps.instruction: Immerse specimens in a graded series of 100% ethanol and 100% HMDS at ratios of 2:1, 1:1, and 1:2 for 10 min each.
Immerse specimens in 100% HMDS for three changes of 15, 30, and 45 min.

steps.title: Dry specimens
steps.instruction: Air dry the specimens in a vacuum desiccator.

substeps.instruction: Cover specimens with fresh 100% HMDS after the final HMDS change.
Move specimens to a vacuum desiccator for air drying at room temperature overnight.

steps.title: Mount and coat specimens
steps.instruction: Prepare specimens for SEM imaging by mounting and sputter coating.

substeps.instruction: Mount the mouthparts and tarsi to stubs.
Coat specimens with 10 nm of gold/palladium in a sputter coater.

steps.title: Perform SEM imaging
steps.instruction: Examine and image the specimens using a scanning electron microscope (Hitachi SU-3500).

substeps.instruction: Photograph the labium and stylets for each developmental stage.
Photograph the tarsal claws and arolia for each developmental stage.
Record the presence or absence of different types of labial sensilla at the labial tip for each developmental stage.
